Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Investments Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Investments' Q2 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Laura Patel, Chief Investment Officer; David Kim, Head of Distribution; Emily Rodriguez, Head of Operations; Robert Hayes, Head of Risk Management; and Nina Gupta, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q2 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust net inflows across channels and continued alpha generation in our active strategies. Our AUM grew to $1.2 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Alex. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Investments delivered strong results in Q2 2024. Our revenue was $950 million, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher performance fees and resilient fee-related earnings amid market appreciation. Our expenses were $312 million, resulting in net income of $285 million. Our expense ratio improved due to scale efficiencies and technology-driven cost savings.

Let me expand on that expense profile. Total operating expenses came in at $312 million for the quarter, up 4.2% from $299 million in Q2 2023. On a full-year 2023 basis, we reported $1.24 billion, or 32.5% of adjusted operating revenues—slightly up from 31.8% the prior year, mainly from investments in technology and talent as AUM expanded to $585 billion by June 30. This reflects tight cost control in a tough macro backdrop with ongoing inflation, Fed rate hikes, and geopolitical pressures on institutional allocations. Our expense-to-revenue ratio stayed under the peer average of 35% per Morningstar, beating out T. Rowe Price and Invesco, whose ratios have edged toward 38% from elevated distribution spending.

Breaking it down: Compensation and benefits, 48% of opex at $150 million quarterly or $595 million trailing twelve months, rose 6.1% year-over-year due to performance incentives linked to 12% AUM growth and $18 billion in net flows to active equity and private markets. Variable pay, including deferred equity under our Long-Term Incentive Plan, made up 55%, rewarding portfolio managers for outperformance like 320 basis points net alpha in our Global Equity Fund over the MSCI World Index. Talent competition with BlackRock and Fidelity pushed base salaries up 4% for investment pros and sign-on bonuses 15% higher for quants. APAC comp grew 8% from Singapore hiring for sovereign mandates, while U.S. held flat via hybrid models post-2023 office cuts. We're capping FY2024 growth at 3-5% through our Pay for Performance 2.0, linking 70% of variable comp to risk-adjusted returns and retention.

Technology and data services, 18% at $56 million quarterly or $224 million TTM, increased 12% year-over-year, now up 200 basis points in mix. This funds AWS cloud for our Apex platform handling $300 billion institutional portfolios, plus AI for ESG in sustainable funds. We spent $25 million on NLP for sentiment from earnings calls, boosting quant signals in our Apex AlphaCore ETF with $2.5 billion YTD flows. Data from Refinitiv and Bloomberg cost $15 million for fixed income amid yield shifts. Europe drove 20% growth for SFDR tech, U.S. cut 10% via vendor deals. Expect 8-10% growth, offset by 15% GenAI efficiencies for $30 million annual savings by Q4.

General and administrative, 16% at $50 million quarterly or $199 million TTM, grew just 1.5%, showing discipline. Occupancy fell 5% after Boston HQ sale-leaseback; professional fees up 3% for audits tied to our $1.2 billion EuroPacific Advisors buy integrating UCITS. Marketing and travel rose 7% to $12 million for private credit roadshows closing $800 million. APAC G&A up 4% for Japan localization amid Abenomics revival, Europe down 2% via Accenture outsourcing. Zero-based budgeting trimmed 8% discretionary, eyeing sub-1% growth in FY2024.

Distribution, servicing, and sub-advisory, 12% at $37 million quarterly or $149 million TTM, up 2.8% with 9% gross flows to Schwab and Vanguard platforms. Rule 12b-1 at 25 bps on retail funds, sub-advisory trails from RIAs added $10 million. U.S. 70%, EMEA up 5% with MiFID II clean shares.

Amortization and other, 6% at $19 million quarterly or $74 million TTM, steady—$12 million non-cash from EuroPacific, $3 million reserves for SEC exams now provisioned, plus D&O insurance up 10% industry-wide.

Overall, opex trailed revenue growth projected at 11% for FY2024, expanding margins 150 bps to 24.5%. We offset 60% inflation via JPMorgan GPO savings and RPA cutting back-office headcount 12%. Q3 opex guidance $305-315 million, FY2024 $1.27-1.29 billion at 2-4% growth and 32% ratio, backing $2.25-$2.35 EPS with M&A scale.

On efficiency ratios, our weighted average expense ratio hit 38 basis points for 2023 across $1.45 trillion AUM, down 12% from 43 bps in 2022—seventh straight decline via scale, tech, and construction. Below Lipper's 52 bps peer average and Morningstar's 61 bps. Passive/ETFs at 42% AUM did 14 bps via ApexFlow; active 62 bps, down 15 bps on shared services; alts 95 bps vs. Blackstone's 120 bps.

U.S. 35 bps from target-date inflows and T+1 shifts; Europe 42 bps aided by MiFID unbundling, despite SFDR; APAC 39 bps via hubs. AUM-per-FTE $285 million up 11%, cost-income 62% with 28% margins. ApexOne platform cut costs 22%, AI research 15%. Direct indexing $60 billion at sub-20 bps grabs 8% affluent share. Guide to 35-36 bps in 2024.

Performance fees hit $285 million in Q2, up 42% quarter-over-quarter, 68% year-over-year—TTM $1.12 billion, 15% of fees. Hedge/liquid alts $162 million with 28% crystallization, 850 bps alpha in market-neutral. Private markets/credit $78 million hitting SOFR+400 bps hurdles. Active equity $45 million on step-ups. Eligible AUM $178 billion, 65% above watermarks; Q3 $300-350 million more.

Performance: 87% AUM beat 1-year benchmarks, 92% 3-year, 89% 5-year; $4.2 billion alpha or 215 bps average. Equities: US large-cap 22.4% vs. S&P 500 20.1% (230 bps), NVIDIA tilt; small/mid 18.7% vs. Russell 2000 15.2%; int'l/EM strong on Japan/India. FI: Agg +5.2% vs. 2.1%; HY 11.4% vs. 9.8%; EM debt solid. Alts: Hedges +13.6% vs. HFRI 8.4%; PE IRRs 24%. Pillars: Quant/AI AlphaForge, ESG tilt, multi-asset positioning.

Organic growth 8.2% Q2, YTD 12.4% vs. industry 4.1%. Flows $28.6 billion, retail $14.2 billion, institutional $14.4 billion. ETFs 14.7%, alts 11.2%. NA 10.1%, EMEA 6.4%, APAC 4.9%. Share: Global 2.6%, US ETFs 3.1%, alts institutional 1.8%. ApexOne sped onboarding, AI personalization lifts retention.

On M&A, inorganic added 4.5 points to 12% growth, $65 billion. EuroAlt Partners $31 billion for 14x EBITDA, accretes 8%, boosts alts to $220 billion. APAC Growth Advisors $13.5 billion at 12.5x, APAC to 15%. Pipeline strong, 2025 6-8% contribution.

Laura Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging quant enhancements and tactical positioning. We launched the Apex AI Equity Fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $2.5 billion in inflows and outperformance versus the S&P 500.

David Kim: Thank you, Laura. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by $15.2 billion aggregate net inflows—11th straight positive quarter, up 28% quarter-over-quarter to YTD $48.7 billion or 4.2% of average AUM, beating peer 2-3%.

Institutional 52% AUM $1.2 trillion, $8.1 billion inflows: Nordic pension $2.5 billion core equity, Gulf SWF $1.8 billion credit. NA 45%, EMEA 36% LDI, APAC Japan REITs. Win rate 62%.

Retail 28% $650 billion, $4.4 billion: ETFs $3.2 billion, GAPG $1.1 billion, Treasury $900 million. US 68%, Europe UCITS, APAC platforms. Digital API boosts stickiness, ESG $50 billion.

Alternatives 20% $460 billion, $2.7 billion: PE $1.4 billion, hedge $800 million, real assets $500 million. EMEA 40%, NA 35%, APAC 25%. GP stakes, blockchain NAV. Diversification 52/28/20, fees 52 bps; Q4 $16-18 billion.

Emily Rodriguez: Thank you, David. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on RPA automation and shared services, cutting headcount needs 12% while migrating to ApexOne for 22% cost reductions in reconciliation and NAV.

Robert Hayes: Thank you, Emily. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and credit spreads and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes stress-testing for Fed pauses and VIX spikes, keeping leverage at 1.2x in credit.

Nina Gupta: Thank you, Robert. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, ApexNext with ML on alt data like satellites, NLP sentiment, and blockchain tokenization for $10 billion privates by 2025, cutting settlement to T+1 and alpha decay 20-30 bps.

Alex Rivera: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes accelerating into alts and ETFs now 42% AUM—private credit 14.2% IRR, new interval funds H1 2025: infra debt $5 billion, RE $3 billion, PE secondaries $2 billion. ETFs five new including crypto basket for 5-7% share. Tech $450 million ApexNext, 150-200 bps alpha. APAC to $15 billion via HK UCITS, EMEA ESG €8 billion, LatAm JV $4 billion. ESG 28% AUM, 150 quants, conservative positioning. Fee earnings $4.2-4.5 billion FY2025 up 11-16%.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your revenue growth this quarter?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, John. Our revenue growth stemmed from a mix of higher average AUM, stable fee rates, and the surge in performance fees we highlighted. Market gains added tailwinds, but organic flows were the core driver.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on your expense management outlook?

Michael Chen: John, as detailed, we're guiding controlled growth with tech offsets. Efficiency gains from ApexOne and GenAI will keep us ahead of inflation and peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morningstar.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Global Equity Fund?

Laura Patel: Good morning, Lisa. The Global Equity Fund returned 22.4% over 12 months, beating the MSCI World by 320 basis points net. Key was our quant rotation into AI semis and Japan reflation, with Sharpe superior across regions.

Lisa Chen: And how is the new product Apex AI Equity Fund performing relative to expectations?

David Kim: It's exceeding, Lisa. $2.5 billion inflows already, 22% YTD vs. S&P 18%, drawing retail and advisors via our digital platforms amid thematic demand.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Patel with JPMorgan.

Mark Patel: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Emily Rodriguez: Thanks, Mark. We've automated 85% of ops on ApexOne, slashing middle/back-office costs 22%—trade recs, NAV, ESG data. RPA reduced headcount needs 12%, robo-advisors under 8 bps, boosting retention.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays.

Robert Lee: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Robert Hayes: Robert, regs like SFDR and MiFID III add reporting costs, but our frameworks integrate seamlessly—TCFD climate scoring, SFDR 8/9 compliance driving inflows. Risk profile stable with conservative leverage and stress tests for QT, elections.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Thompson with Morningstar.

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your AUM outlook. With markets volatile amid Fed rate cut expectations and geopolitical headwinds, can management walk us through the drivers for AUM growth over the next 12-18 months? Specifically, how do you see net flows breaking down by asset class and region, and what role will your tech initiatives play?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, Sarah. Happy to provide some color on our AUM trajectory. We closed Q2 with record AUM of $1.2 trillion, up 12% quarter-over-quarter and 22% year-over-year. This reflects $18 billion in long-term net inflows—our strongest quarter since Q4 2021—coupled with 7% market appreciation and modest FX tailwinds from a weaker USD against the euro and yen.

For FY2024, we're guiding 8-10% AUM growth to $1.3-1.32 trillion end-year. Assumes S&P 5-7%, bonds 3-4%, 5-7% organic from $65-75 billion inflows. Equities 40% flows, Global Alpha 15% YTD +400 bps MSCI; ETFs $12 billion Q2 like GAIE. FI $20-25 billion short-duration; alts $15-20 billion private credit 9-11% IRR.

NA 62% AUM $40-45 billion RIAs; Europe 22% 10-12% UCITS ETFs €5 billion; APAC 12% 15-20% YoY $8-10 billion China/Japan JV Nomura; LatAm/ME opportunistic.

Pillars: Innovation—three Q4 ETFs AI, income, ESG; tech AlphaForge live 40% equities +20-30 bps, AlphaWealth $15 billion; expansion M&A boutiques, stable 42 bps fees, Target Return 7%. Risks hedged beta 0.85, duration 4.2. Constructive to 12-15% CAGR 2027.

Back to you, operator.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Investments. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
